newsitem.title: CHINA: China supports Boutros-Ghali U.N. re-election bid.
newsitem.headline: China supports Boutros-Ghali U.N. re-election bid.

text.p: China on Monday threw its weight behind Boutros Boutros-Ghali's bid to be re-elected as Secretary-General of the United Nations.

The United States has said it was ready to veto a second five-year term for the 74-year-old Egyptian diplomat. On Monday, the Security Council was expected to begin nominating a U.N. chief to lead the world body into the next century.
Beijing's move came one day before the arrival of U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher for a three-day visit.
China said it was happy with Boutros-Ghali.

"China appraises positively the important work by Mr Boutros-Ghali to strengthen the role of the United Nations during his tenure as U.N. Secretary-General," the official Xinhua news agency said, quoting Foreign Ministry spokesman Cui Tiankai.
Beijing said it backed the stance of the Organisation of African Unity (OAU) on Boutros-Ghali's candidacy.
"The OAU's recommendation of Mr Boutros-Ghali for re-election is justified and we will support it," Cui said.
China's state media have accused the United States of "flaunting high-handedness" and trying to dominate the United Nations by attempting to block the re-election of Boutros-Ghali.
